lessons.title: Find Your Way Around
lessons.subtitle: Layers, controls and the menu
lessons.pitch: Layers in a stack, a panel for the one you picked, and one menu. The whole Pro Editor in a pass.
outcomes: Hide a layer and bring it back
Find a layer's Adjust, Blend and Mask
Find Hide Edits, the histogram, Undo and Crop

steps.text: Your photo is never touched. Every edit is a [[layer]] on top of it.
Open Layers and tap the eye beside Exposure: that edit stops showing.
Show it again. Tap its name and close Layers: its panel opens.
Adjust holds its controls, Blend how it mixes, Mask where it works.
Open the dots menu: Hide Edits, Pipeline, Save as Look and more.
Pick Hide Edits to see the original. Show Edits brings them back.
The graph up top is the [[histogram]]: dark on the left, bright on the right.
Undo steps back, Redo steps forward. Undo once, then Redo.
[[crop|Crop]] lives on the photo. In Layers, tap Image, then close Layers.
Swipe the photo's row to the left and tap the crop icon.
steps.wide: Tap the photo's row to unfold it, then tap Crop.

steps.text: That is the editor: a stack, a panel for the layer you picked, one menu.

lessons.title: Your First Edit
lessons.subtitle: Add a layer, change it, take it back
lessons.pitch: Every edit is a layer. Add one, change it, take it off. That is the whole idea.
outcomes: Add an adjustment layer with +
Move Exposure and watch the photo follow
Hide a layer with the eye, bring it back

steps.text: Every edit here is a [[layer]]: add one, change it, take it off.
Tap + and pick [[exposure|Exposure]]: the whole photo, brighter or darker.
Drag Exposure up or down; the photo follows. No number is wrong.
steps.wide: Drag Exposure left or right and watch the photo follow. No number is wrong.

steps.text: In Layers, tap its eye to hide it, then again to show it. The photo is safe.
Add, change, take back: that is the loop. Every tool is another layer.

lessons.title: Light and Shadow
lessons.subtitle: Move one end without moving the other
lessons.pitch: The shade went very dark. Tone opens one end of the range without moving the other.
outcomes: Open the shadows without touching the highlights
Set where the darkest tone lands with Blacks
Know when Tone beats Exposure

steps.text: The shade went very dark. Exposure would brighten the sunlit wall too.
Tap + and pick [[tone|Tone]] instead. It moves one end at a time.
Raise Shadows. The shade opens up; the sunlit wall stays as it was.
Blacks sets the darkest tone. Lower it a touch if the shade looks milky.
Tone moves one end at a time. Exposure moves the whole range.

lessons.title: Give It Some Contrast
lessons.subtitle: The S curve, and why it works
lessons.pitch: A flat photo bunches in the middle. One S on the curve spreads the tones apart.
outcomes: Read flatness on the histogram
Pull an S curve by hand
See why a steeper middle spreads the tones

steps.text: This shot is flat: its [[histogram]] bunches up, and none of it is white.
Tap + and pick [[curves|Curves]]: it moves dark and bright apart.
Tap the line low, drag the new point down. Tap it high, drag that one up.
Look at the histogram again: it has spread toward both walls.
The S steepens the middle and pulls tones apart. That is contrast.

lessons.title: Levels, Step by Step
lessons.subtitle: Set the ends, bend the middle, fade the black
lessons.pitch: Curves' job in five controls: set the ends, bend the middle, fade the black.
outcomes: Set the black and white points where the hill starts
Bend the midtones with Gamma
Fade the blacks with Output Black

steps.text: Tap + and pick [[levels|Levels]]. Its graph is the [[histogram]] of the photo.
Drag Black and White in to the ends of the hill. The haze lifts.
Gamma bends the midtones, not the ends. Slide it right to brighten them.
Slide Output Black right: the darkest tone turns gray, a faded film look.
Two set the ends, one bends the middle, two fade the result: Levels.

lessons.title: Color Without Overdoing It
lessons.subtitle: Why Vibrance and Saturation are not the same control
lessons.pitch: Two controls make color stronger. One turns every color up; the other lifts the dull ones.
outcomes: See what each does to dull and loud colors
Reach for Vibrance first
Use Saturation only when you mean everything

steps.text: Two controls make color stronger. Tap + and pick [[vibrance|Vibrance]].
Raise Saturation hard. Everything gets louder, the face included.
Tap Saturation, type 0 and tap Done. Then raise Vibrance just as far.
Vibrance lifts the dull coat, not the loud peonies. Saturation lifts both.
Reach for Vibrance first. Saturation is for when you want everything.

lessons.title: Fix the Color Cast
lessons.subtitle: Name the light, and take its color back out
lessons.pitch: Bulbs paint a room orange, shade paints it blue. White Balance takes that color back out.
outcomes: Spot a color cast on something white
Undo a light's color with one tap
Fine-tune with Temperature and Tint

steps.text: Warm bulbs turned this cafe yellow. Tap + and pick [[white_balance|White Balance]].
At the top of its panel, tap the bulb: it takes most of that yellow out.
Fine-tune with Temperature: toward Cool until the cups read white.
Tint does the same between green and magenta, for some lamps' cast.
Name the light, take its color out, then choose how warm to go.

lessons.title: One Color at a Time
lessons.subtitle: Change a single color and leave the rest
lessons.pitch: A blue door in a street of colors: change that one and leave everything else as it was.
outcomes: Add a color to Hue & Saturation
Shift one hue without touching the rest
Mute or deepen just that color

steps.text: Tap + and pick [[hue_saturation|Hue & Saturation]]. Alone, it moves every color.
Tap + among its colors and add Blues: now it acts on blue alone.
Drag Hue up or down: the door changes, the red flowers do not.
steps.wide: Drag Hue left or right: the door changes color, the red flowers do not.

steps.text: Saturation and Lightness work the same, on blue only. Try muting it.
Master moves every color; an added one moves only itself.

lessons.title: Black & White, on Purpose
lessons.subtitle: Gray is a decision you make per color
lessons.pitch: Gray is not one recipe. Decide what each color is worth, one control at a time.
outcomes: Convert to gray and keep control per color
Darken a blue sky, lift a red subject
Change the subject of a photo with two controls

steps.text: Gray is not one recipe. Tap + and pick [[black_white|Black & White]].
Each color has its own control: how light it turns in gray.
Lower Blues. Everything blue goes dark; here that is the whole sky.
Raise Reds, then drag the panel down: the tram turns bright.
steps.wide: Now raise Reds: the tram turns bright. Same photo, a new subject.

steps.text: Color did not vanish. You decided what each one is worth in gray.

lessons.title: Detail, Without the Crunch
lessons.subtitle: Five controls, five different jobs
lessons.pitch: Sharpen, Clarity, Texture, Dehaze, Denoise: five jobs in one layer. Push each past its limit.
outcomes: Sharpen until the edges bite, then stop
Tell Clarity from Texture
Cut haze, then back Denoise off before plastic

steps.text: Five controls all sound like more detail. Tap + and pick [[detail|Detail]].
Raise Sharpen until the sweater's knit bites, then stop.
Clarity adds punch to the shapes; Texture brings out the grain in them.
Dehaze firms up the far mountains. Stop before the face looks heavy.
Push Denoise all the way: the face turns to plastic. Back off.
Edges, shapes, grain, air, speckle: five jobs. Use each a little.

lessons.title: Lead the Eye
lessons.subtitle: A vignette, then Opacity to set its strength
lessons.pitch: Darker edges pull the eye to the middle. Opacity, on every layer, decides how much.
outcomes: Darken the edges with Vignette
Move where the darkening starts with Midpoint
Set any layer's strength with Opacity

steps.text: So much bright stone, one red umbrella. Tap + and pick [[vignette|Vignette]].
Drag the first slider toward D, for Darken. The umbrella stands out.
steps.wide: Drag the top slider toward Darken. The edges sink; the umbrella stands out.

steps.text: Midpoint sets where the darkening starts. Move it until no edge shows.
Open the Blend page and lower [[opacity|Opacity]]: the vignette fades evenly.
A good vignette is felt, not seen. And Opacity is every layer's volume.

lessons.title: Start from a Filter
lessons.subtitle: A filter is a layer too, with its own strength
lessons.pitch: Pick a filter for the mood, then dial it back. It is a layer like any other.
outcomes: Add a Filters layer and pick a filter
Set its strength with Intensity
Compare with the eye, keep it or drop it

steps.text: Tap + and pick [[filters|Filters]]. A filter is a whole grade in one layer.
Pick a filter in its panel. Try a few: each one replaces the last.
Lower Intensity until it suits. Most look best well under full strength.
In Layers, tap its eye to compare with the photo, then show it again.
A filter is a starting point you can turn down. The rest stays yours.

lessons.title: Look Inside a Look
lessons.subtitle: A look is ordinary layers, kept as one
lessons.pitch: A look is ordinary layers, kept as one. Ungroup it, weaken one, change another.
outcomes: See what a look is made of
Turn a look into a folder you can change
Weaken one grade with Opacity, keep the rest

steps.text: This photo opens on a [[look|look]]. Open Layers and see what it holds.
Four ordinary layers, kept together. A look stays as it was made.
Tap its Gradient Map, then Ungroup Into a Folder. Each layer is yours.
On the Gradient Map's Blend page, lower [[opacity|Opacity]]. That grade fades.
In Layers, tap Color Balance, close Layers. Slide its Blue to Yellow.
A look is a start: ungroup any look and its layers are yours to change.

lessons.title: Darken the Sky
lessons.subtitle: Curves under a gradient mask, the way a landscape is graded
lessons.pitch: One layer, one curve, one mask: darken the sky and let the land stay.
outcomes: Darken with a Curves layer
Add a gradient mask and drag it into place
Keep the ground untouched while the sky drops

steps.text: Every change lives on its own [[layer]]. Tap + and pick [[curves|Curves]].
Tap the middle of the line, drag it down. Sky and land darken alike.
Open its Mask page and tap Gradient.
Red stays untouched. Drag the lower dot down to the horizon.
Now drag the top dot down near it, until the land is red again.
One [[layer]], one curve, one [[mask]]: that is the whole move.
